title: Blunder check
summary: Ask three short questions before every move and stop the simple blunders.
body:
### Check before you move

Most games at your level end because of one big mistake. A piece is left alone, or a free capture is missed. You can stop this with one short habit.

Before every move, ask three questions:

- What does my opponent threaten now?
- Which of my pieces can be taken for free?
- Does my move leave a piece alone?

Look at the **last move** your opponent made. It often shows a new threat. A queen that moved to a new square may attack your pieces. A bishop that moved may open a line to your king.

Then look at the square where your piece will land. Ask yourself if an enemy piece can take it. If a pawn can take it, the square is usually not safe.

This check takes only a few seconds. You will not find every danger. But you will stop most simple blunders, and that wins many games.

Rule of thumb: before you press the move, say out loud what your opponent can take after it.

Practise this on each move of your next game. Soon it will feel normal and fast.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Find the checkmate.
exercises.explanation: The queen takes f7. The bishop on c4 guards it, so the king cannot take back.
The black queen has no guard. The rook takes it for free.

exercises.prompt: Black to move. Find the checkmate.
exercises.explanation: The white king has no escape. The queen on h4 gives checkmate.
